title: ZIA Terraform provider authentication, client modes and rate limiting

prose.text: The ZIA Terraform provider supports OneAPI and the legacy framework, and has a no-credential mode and its own rate-limit handling. {{legacy-compat-since-4-0}}

prose.label: Sandbox credentials.
prose.text: {{sandbox-auth-variables}} The legacy variables are no longer supported, and a resource page still names them: [[zia.terraform.sandbox-resources:sandbox-token-variable-names]].

prose.label: Rate limiting.
prose.text: {{retry-after-transparent}} {{keep-default-parallelism}} {{parallelism-ignored}} {{static-ip-post-1-per-second}} {{static-ip-legacy-rate-row}} Whether the OneAPI endpoint has the same limit is open {{gap:static-ip-oneapi-limit}}. {{provider-default-retries-100}}

prose.label: Write lock.
prose.text: {{write-lock-is-not-rate-limit}} How applies compete for that lock: [[zia.terraform.activation-methods]].

checks.do: Whether a provider that errors on every resource was configured with `skip_credentials_validation`, which builds no client.
Whether a 409 on a write is tenant write-lock contention rather than rate limiting before changing the run's parallelism.
Whether the provider version is at least v4.7.25 before configuring a FedRAMP cloud.

legacy-compat-since-4-0.statement: Since provider v4.0.0 the ZIA provider offers backwards compatibility with the legacy Zscaler API framework alongside OneAPI.

quotes: As of version v4.0.0, this Terraform provider offers backwards compatibility to the Zscaler legacy API framework.
evidence.after: The ZIA Terraform Provider now offers support for [OneAPI]

fedramp-gov-values.statement: OneAPI reaches the government (FedRAMP) clouds through the `gov` and `govus` cloud values, and the provider documents this as supported only from v4.7.25; earlier versions are not supported.

quotes: Supported Zidentity Gov Cloud `gov` or `govus`
FedRAMP cloud is only supported when upgrading to the provider version `>=v4.7.25`. Earlier versions are NOT supported.

skip-credentials-builds-no-client.statement: With `skip_credentials_validation` (or `ZSCALER_SKIP_CREDENTIALS_VALIDATION`) the provider skips credential validation and never builds the API client, because the OneAPI SDK performs an OAuth handshake in its constructor.

quotes: Skip credentials validation and API client initialization entirely.
// The OneAPI SDK performs an OAuth handshake inside its constructor, // so "skipping validation" means never building the client.
} else if os.Getenv("ZSCALER_SKIP_CREDENTIALS_VALIDATION") != "" {

skip-credentials-intended-use.statement: The documented use of `skip_credentials_validation` is a configuration in which every `zia_*` resource and data source is conditionally disabled (for example `count = 0`); plan and apply then succeed with a warning even without credentials.

quotes: - `skip_credentials_validation` - (Optional) When set to `true`, the provider skips credential validation and does not initialize the API client.
This is intended for configurations where the ZIA provider is declared but every `zia_*` resource and data source is conditionally disabled (e.g., `count = 0`)
With this flag enabled, `terraform plan`/`apply` succeeds with a warning even when no credentials are supplied

skip-credentials-calls-fail.statement: With that flag set, every resource and data source CRUD function is wrapped so that one which does attempt an API call returns an explanatory error instead of dereferencing a nil service.

quotes: for _, r := range p.ResourcesMap { guardResourceAgainstInertClient(r) }
for _, ds := range p.DataSourcesMap { guardResourceAgainstInertClient(ds) }
// guardResourceAgainstInertClient wraps a resource's CRUD and import // functions so that, in skip_credentials_validation mode, they return a
return a descriptive error instead of dereferencing the nil Service.

skip-credentials-since-4-8-7.statement: The `skip_credentials_validation` attribute was added in provider v4.8.7.

quotes: Added the provider attribute `skip_credentials_validation`

sandbox-auth-variables.statement: Sandbox authentication uses its own token and cloud, set through `ZSCALER_SANDBOX_TOKEN` and `ZSCALER_SANDBOX_CLOUD` or the `sandbox_token` and `sandbox_cloud` attributes.

quotes: requires the following new environment variables the `ZSCALER_SANDBOX_CLOUD` and `ZSCALER_SANDBOX_TOKEN` or authentication attributes `sandbox_token` and `sandbox_cloud`

parallelism-ignored.statement: The provider-block `parallelism` attribute is deprecated and ignored.

quotes: "parallelism": { Type: schema.TypeInt, Optional: true,
Deprecated and ignored. Previously limited the number of concurrent API requests.

retry-after-transparent.statement: When ZIA answers HTTP 429, the provider waits the interval in the `Retry-After` header and retries the request transparently, so exceeding a rate limit costs a delay rather than a failed apply.

quotes: the provider waits the indicated interval and retries the request transparently
the provider honours the Retry-After header returned on a 429 response and retries transparently.

keep-default-parallelism.statement: The provider documentation says to run Terraform with its default settings, with nothing to configure to stay within the rate limits.

quotes: Run Terraform with its default settings.
You do not need to configure anything to stay within these limits.

write-lock-is-not-rate-limit.statement: An HTTP 409 reporting `EDIT_LOCK_NOT_AVAILABLE` or `Failed during enter Org barrier` means another session is modifying the configuration, not that a rate limit was exceeded.

quotes: An `HTTP 409` response reporting `EDIT_LOCK_NOT_AVAILABLE` or `Failed during enter Org barrier` indicates that another session is modifying the configuration, not that a rate limit was exceeded.

static-ip-post-1-per-second.statement: The provider documentation gives `/staticIP` as an example of an endpoint limited to 1 POST request per second, while some endpoints allow several per second.

quotes: some endpoints allow multiple POST requests per second, while others (such as `/staticIP`) are limited to 1 POST request per second.

provider-tracks-public-api.statement: The provider maintains parity with publicly available API endpoints, so a feature visible in the Zscaler UI but not yet in the API cannot be in the provider.

quotes: The ZIA Terraform provider maintain parity with publicly available API endpoints.

object-presence-not-entitlement.statement: So the presence of a Terraform resource or data source shows API coverage, not that a given tenant is entitled to or has enabled the feature.
object-presence-not-entitlement.conditions: Inferred: provider coverage follows the public API, and entitlement is a property of the tenant. Resources that are subscription-gated (ISOLATE) or Early Access are still present in the provider.

static-ip-legacy-rate-row.statement: Zscaler's legacy ZIA API rate limit summary lists /staticIP at 2/sec and 1000/hr for GET and 1/sec and 400/hr for POST (a resource URI by method table).

quotes: | Resource URI | GET (read) | POST (create) | PUT (replace) | DELETE |
| /staticIP | 2/sec and 1000/hr | 1/sec and 400/hr | - | - |

provider-default-retries-100.statement: The Terraform ZIA provider sets its own default retry count of 100, which its source describes as deliberately above the SDK default so that bulk applies survive sustained rate limiting.

quotes: retryCount:     100, // Deliberately above the SDK default so bulk applies survive sustained rate limiting.

static-ip-oneapi-limit.title: Whether the OneAPI /staticIP endpoint carries the same limit as the legacy table
static-ip-oneapi-limit.detail: The per-endpoint limit appears in the legacy API rate limit summary and in the provider guide, but the OneAPI rate-limiting guide for ZIA is not among the captured sources, so whether the OneAPI endpoint the provider uses by default has the same figure is not confirmed against a primary OneAPI table or a live bulk-POST test.
static-ip-oneapi-limit.blocks: treating the legacy figure as the limit that applies to OneAPI-based Terraform runs
